# hatchway

A narrow, logged opening through which an outside agent reaches your tools.

```bash
pip install hatchway
hatchway authorize "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... my-agent" --agent assistant   # one confined key
hatchway check "crowsnest triage"                                     # what the gate would do
```

An agent that lives somewhere else (a personal assistant on its own cloud VM, another machine’s scheduler, a phone shortcut) gets one SSH key. That key can do exactly one thing: run `hatchway gate`, which reads the requested command line, checks it against a **profile** (an allowlist kept as a TOML file), logs the call, and runs the allowed command directly, never through a shell. Anything not in the profile is refused with a reason.

It is the “reach in” half of connecting an outside agent to the tools on your machine, with no new server, no open port and no new dependency: OpenSSH already has forced commands, and hatchway is the policy and the bookkeeping around one.

## What you get

- **An allowlist as data.** A rule names the words the agent sends, the command that actually runs (with fixed arguments the agent cannot remove, such as `--no-verify`), and exactly which flags and names it may add. Names are checked against a pattern and passed after `--`, so they can never be read as options. Shell characters are refused outright.
- **A confined key.** `hatchway authorize` writes one `authorized_keys` line with `command="hatchway gate --agent NAME"`, `restrict` (no shell, no port, agent or X11 forwarding, no pty), and by default `from="100.64.0.0/10,fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48"`, so the key works only from a Tailscale tailnet even if sshd is reachable elsewhere. It keeps every other line, backs the file up first, and is idempotent. `hatchway revoke --agent NAME` takes it out.
- **A log of every call** in `~/.local/share/hatchway/calls.jsonl`: when, which agent, from where, what was asked, allowed or refused, exit status. Never the output. `hatchway log` shows the tail.
- **Gated classes.** A rule can belong to a class that stays off until a flag file exists. The bundled profile’s `dispatch` class (starting a Claude Code session) needs both `~/.config/hatchway/allow-dispatch` and a list of directories it may start sessions in.
- **A snapshot for pulling instead of waiting.** `hatchway snapshot` runs the profile’s snapshot requests (through the same allowlist) and writes the answers atomically to `~/.local/share/hatchway/out/`, with an `index.json`. The agent reads them through the gate (`snapshot triage.md`) without waiting for anything to run. `hatchway schedule --every 300` keeps them fresh with launchd (macOS) or a systemd user timer (Linux).
- **Skills for the agents that set it up.** `hatchway install-skills` links the bundled skills into one or more Claude Code homes.

## The bundled profile: `claude-fleet`

For a machine running Claude Code sessions watched by [crowsnest](https://github.com/thorwhalen/crowsnest) (live sessions) and [openloops](https://github.com/thorwhalen/openloops) (what sessions left owed or blocked). `hatchway help` prints it, and it is what the agent gets when it sends `help`:

| Request                                                                                    | Runs                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `crowsnest [--brief|--json]`                                                               | the roster across every configured Claude home                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `crowsnest triage [-q] [--json]`                                                           | what needs you, what is safe to close, what is working                                                                                                                                                            |
| `crowsnest show|turns|recap|brief NAME`                                                    | one session (show and turns quote its transcript)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `crowsnest ledger [NAME...]`, `groups`, `synopsis GROUP`, `questions`, `lineage`, `report` | the rest of crowsnest’s read side                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ol`, `ol owed`, `ol blocked`, `ol dashboard`                                              | openloops; `owed` and `dashboard` always with `--no-verify` (verify predicates are commands taken from issue bodies, and a remote request never runs them); `blocked` runs no predicate, so it takes no such flag |
| `snapshot [FILE]`                                                                          | list or print the snapshot files                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `crowsnest spawn NAME --cwd DIR --prompt TEXT`                                             | **gated**: starts a session on `sonnet`, in a directory under the dispatch roots                                                                                                                                  |

Nothing in it kills, reaps, messages or writes into a running session.

To change it for one machine, copy `hatchway/data/profiles/claude-fleet.toml` to `~/.config/hatchway/profiles/<name>.toml`, edit it, and set `profile = "<name>"` in `~/.config/hatchway/config.toml` (or pass `--profile <name>` to `authorize`, which puts it in that key’s forced command).

## The second transport: MCP

The same profile can be served as MCP tools, for an agent that speaks MCP but cannot open SSH (a claude.ai custom connector, so also the Claude app’s voice mode; Claude Desktop; another machine’s MCP client). One tool per rule: its `tool` name, its flags and names as typed parameters, its `help` as the description. Every call is turned back into the request words and goes through the gate, so it is decided, logged and locked exactly as an SSH call is.

```bash
pip install 'hatchway[mcp]'
hatchway mcp --profile claude-ai --list                    # the tools, with their signatures
hatchway mcp --profile claude-ai --http 8799               # serve on 127.0.0.1:8799/mcp
hatchway mcp --profile claude-ai --ssh me@laptop --identity key   # each call through that machine's gate
```

```python
from hatchway.mcp import fan_out, mk_server, routed_runner, ssh_runner, with_fallback

server = ssh_runner("root@127.0.0.1", identity="key")  # this machine, as another user
laptop = ssh_runner(
    "me@127.0.0.1", identity="key", ssh=("ssh", "-T", "-p", "2222")
)  # through a tunnel
runner = routed_runner(server, {"crowsnest": with_fallback(laptop, server)})
# or ask every machine at once and merge, each row tagged [laptop] / [server]:
runner = routed_runner(server, {"crowsnest": fan_out({"laptop": laptop, "server": server})})
app = mk_server("claude-ai", runner=runner, auth=..., classes=("read", "handoff")).http_app()
```

The *runner* is the seam: `local_runner` runs the gate on this machine; `ssh_runner` sends the request to a key whose forced command is the gate, so a server process running as its own account reaches tools it holds no credentials for. `routed_runner` sends a request to the runner of the longest leading words it matches (`"crowsnest"`, `"crowsnest intent"`); `with_fallback` asks a second machine only when the first cannot be reached; `fan_out` asks several machines in parallel and merges their answers, each line tagged with its machine, and names on its own line any machine that did not answer, so a partial list never reads as a whole one. Use it for reads only: a request that changes something goes to one runner. A rule’s `reply` (a template over `{out}`, the command’s output) shapes a successful answer for these transports, as `post_handoff` does to return a line to paste into Claude Code. Authentication is the job of whoever serves it on a network (`auth=` goes to `FastMCP`). Only the classes you name are offered (default: `read`). Long answers are paged: every tool takes `offset`, and the answer says where to resume.

**The bundled `claude-ai` profile** is shaped for a conversation, typed or spoken: Claude Code sessions (`session_triage`, `session_roster`, `session_recap`, `session_turns`, `session_ledger`), open loops (`owed_by_owner`, `blocked_work`), GitHub read-only (`list_repos`, `repo_overview`, `read_repo_file`, `list_issues`, `read_issue`; a repository whose name contains `secret` is refused), and a handoff inbox shared with Claude Code through [annals](https://github.com/thorwhalen/annals) (`read_handoffs`, `read_document` and `document_info`, which take an annals link as handed, on any annals the machine’s annals config can read, and `post_handoff` in the `handoff` class, whose text goes to the command’s standard input, never its arguments). A machine adds what only it has in a private profile that starts with `extends = "claude-ai"`.

## Configuration

`~/.config/hatchway/config.toml`, every key optional:

```toml
profile = "claude-fleet"
path = ["~/.local/bin"]           # where the commands live (sshd's PATH is minimal)
timeout = 120
[roots]                           # extra directories file rules may serve, by name
[dispatch]
roots = ["~/projects"]            # where a gated spawn may start a session
[snapshot]
to = ""                           # optional private copy: a local dir or host:path
```

## The security model, in one paragraph

What the key can do is the profile, so read it before you authorise a key. Read commands still send what they read to wherever the agent runs: `crowsnest show` quotes your sessions’ transcripts, so authorise only an agent you would show them to. Keep the `from=` restriction. If the agent joins your Tailscale tailnet, give it a policy that allows **only TCP port 22** to the machines it serves and **no Tailscale SSH rule**: Tailscale SSH authenticates by tailnet identity and never reads `authorized_keys`, so it would bypass the gate entirely. `100.64.0.0/10` is also ordinary carrier-grade NAT space, so once you know the agent’s own tailnet address, narrow `--from` to it (`--from 100.x.y.z/32`). Leave dispatch off until you have watched the log for a while: a session it starts runs code as you. The bundled rule pins `--model sonnet` and `--permission-mode default` (the session asks before acting), refuses a prompt that starts with `-`, and starts sessions only under the directories you list.

Also built in: the commands run with an allowlisted environment (nothing the connecting client can set reaches them beyond `LANG`), in their own process group so a timeout stops their children too, one call at a time per agent (a concurrent call is refused with exit 75), and every allowed call is logged before it runs, so a dropped connection still leaves its line.

## Agents

- `hatchway` skill: install and verify a connection for an outside agent on this machine (the steps, the checks, the Tailscale policy).
- `hatchway-muse` skill: when a task would be better handed to a personal Muse agent (Meta), which integration pattern fits, and the exact prompt to give it.

# _autosummary/hatchway.config.html.md

# hatchway.config

Where hatchway keeps its configuration and its records, and how a profile is found.

Config: `$HATCHWAY_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.config/hatchway/` (`config.toml`, the flag
files such as `allow-dispatch`, optional user profiles in `profiles/`).
Data: `$HATCHWAY_DATA_DIR` or `~/.local/share/hatchway/` (`calls.jsonl`, the
snapshot in `out/`, backups of files hatchway edited in `backups/`).

The config file is optional; every key has a default:

```default
profile = "claude-fleet"      # a bundled profile name, or a path to a .toml
path = ["/opt/bin"]           # prepended to PATH for the commands the gate runs
timeout = 120                 # seconds before a command is stopped
[roots]                       # directories file rules may serve, by name
ledger = "~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger"
[dispatch]
roots = ["~/projects"]        # where a dispatch (spawn) may start a session
[snapshot]
to = ""                       # optional extra copy: a local dir or host:path (rsync)
```

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| `load_profile`([name_or_path, settings])                                                    |                                                                                                     |

### Classes

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/hatchway.html.md

# hatchway

hatchway: a narrow, logged opening through which an outside agent reaches your tools.

An agent that lives elsewhere (a personal assistant on its own cloud VM, a phone
shortcut, another machine’s scheduler) gets one SSH key. That key can do one thing:
run [`gate()`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.gate), which reads the requested command line, checks it against a profile
(an allowlist kept as data), logs it, and runs it without a shell, or refuses.

```pycon
>>> from hatchway import decide, load_profile
>>> profile = load_profile("claude-fleet")
>>> decide("crowsnest triage --quiet", profile).allowed
True
>>> decide("crowsnest spawn x --prompt hi", profile).allowed   # gated off by default
False
```

### Functions

| [`authorize`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.authorize)(public_key, \*, agent[, profile, ...])   | Add (or confirm) the gate's line for `public_key`, keeping every other line.                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`decide`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.decide)(request, profile, \*[, flags_present, ...]) | Decide what to do with `request` (the agent's command line, as SSH hands it).                       |
| [`describe`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.describe)(profile)                                  | One line per rule, for the `help` answer an agent gets.                                             |
| [`gate`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.gate)([request, agent, profile, settings])          | Decide and run one request.                                                                         |
| [`install_schedule`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.install_schedule)(\*[, every, dry_run])             | Write the units and load them (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux).                          |
| [`install_skills`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.install_skills)(\*[, homes, force, dry_run])        | Link the bundled skills (and agents, if any) into each Claude home.                                 |
| [`key_line`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.key_line)(public_key, \*, agent[, profile, ...])    | The `authorized_keys` line that confines `public_key` to the gate.                                  |
| `load_profile`([name_or_path, settings])                                                            |                                                                                                     |
| [`load_settings`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.load_settings)(\*[, config_file])                   | Read `config.toml` (absent is fine) into [`Settings`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.Settings). |
| [`revoke`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.revoke)(agent, \*[, authorized_keys, dry_run, ...]) | Remove every line whose forced command is the gate for `agent`.                                     |
| [`snapshot`](_autosummary/hatchway.html.md#hatchway.snapshot)(\*[, profile, settings])                  | Run every snapshot request once; return the index that was written.                                 |

### Classes

### *class* hatchway.Decision(allowed, request, reason='', rule=None, argv=(), path='', stdin=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What the gate does with a request: run `argv`, print `path`, or refuse.

### *class* hatchway.Profile(rules, classes=dict(), name='', snapshot=(), instructions='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A named set of rules plus the gating of their classes.

#### rule_for(tokens)

The rule with the longest `match` that prefixes `tokens`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Rule`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Rule) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *class* hatchway.Rule(match, argv=(), kind='exec', klass='read', flags=frozenset({}), value_flags=(), max_positional=0, min_positional=0, positional_pattern='[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@:+-]{0,127}', root='', help='', tool='', arg='', param='', stdin='', reply='', tail=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One allowed command shape.

`kind` is `exec` (run `argv` plus the checked extras) or `file` (print one
file, named by the single positional argument, from the directory `root`).
`klass` groups rules for gating: a class listed in the profile’s `[classes]`
table with `requires_flag` is refused until that flag file exists.

`tool`, `param` and `arg` only name things for other transports (the MCP
tool’s name, its positional parameter’s name and that parameter’s description); `stdin` names a `free` value flag
whose value is written to the command’s standard input instead of its arguments,
so a body of text (a note to publish) never lands in `argv`. `reply` shapes a
successful answer for those transports: a template whose only field is `{out}`, the
command’s output stripped (a published link turned into a line to paste elsewhere).
`tail` is fixed words placed after the request’s arguments (`-`, for a command
that reads its text from standard input only in that position).

### *class* hatchway.Settings(profile='claude-fleet', path=list(), timeout=120, roots=dict(), dispatch_roots=list(), snapshot_to='', config_dir=config_dir(), data_dir=data_dir())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The resolved configuration the gate and the snapshot run with.

#### all_roots()

File-rule roots: `out` (the snapshot) always, plus the configured ones.

Add (or confirm) the gate’s line for `public_key`, keeping every other line.

Returns `{"action": "added" | "ok" | "replaced" | "conflict", ...}`. A line for the
same key with different options is a `conflict` unless `replace`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### hatchway.decide(request, profile, , flags_present=frozenset({}), dispatch_roots=(), roots=None)

Decide what to do with `request` (the agent’s command line, as SSH hands it).

`flags_present` names the flag files that exist (a gated class needs its flag);
`dispatch_roots` are the directories a `path_under_roots` value must sit in;
`roots` maps a file rule’s `root` name to a directory.

```pycon
>>> p = Profile.from_dict({"rule": [
...     {"match": ["snapshot"], "kind": "file", "root": "out"}]})
>>> decide("snapshot ../../.ssh/id_ed25519", p, roots={"out": "/tmp/o"}).allowed
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Decision`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Decision)

One line per rule, for the `help` answer an agent gets.

* **Return type:**

Decide and run one request. `request` defaults to `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`.

### hatchway.install_skills(, homes=None, force=False, dry_run=False)

# _autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md

# hatchway.install

Putting a hatch on a machine: the `authorized_keys` line, the snapshot timer, the skills.

Every function here is idempotent, backs a file up before changing it (into
`<data>/backups/`), and has a `dry_run` that says what it would do.

### Functions

| [`authorize`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.authorize)(public_key, \*, agent[, profile, ...])   | Add (or confirm) the gate's line for `public_key`, keeping every other line.                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `backup`(path, \*, settings)                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                |
| [`claude_homes`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.claude_homes)()                                     | Every Claude Code home here: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-*` with a skills folder.                                                               |
| [`hatchway_bin`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.hatchway_bin)()                                     | The absolute path of this install's `hatchway` script, for the forced command.                                                                 |
| [`install_schedule`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.install_schedule)(\*[, every, dry_run])             | Write the units and load them (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux).                                                                     |
| [`install_skills`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.install_skills)(\*[, homes, force, dry_run])        | Link the bundled skills (and agents, if any) into each Claude home.                                                                            |
| [`key_line`](_autosummary/hatchway.install.html.md#hatchway.install.key_line)(public_key, \*, agent[, profile, ...])    | The `authorized_keys` line that confines `public_key` to the gate.                                                                             |

# _autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md

# hatchway.mcp

The second transport: a profile served as MCP tools, one tool per rule.

The SSH gate is the way in for an agent that can open SSH. An agent that speaks MCP but
cannot (a claude.ai custom connector, Claude Desktop, another machine’s MCP client) gets
the same allowlist here: each rule of the profile becomes one tool whose parameters are
the rule’s flags and names, and every call is turned back into the request words and
handed to a *runner*, which takes it through the gate. So the same `decide()`, the same
log, the same gated classes, the same one-call-at-a-time lock, whichever way it arrived.

```pycon
>>> from hatchway.policy import Profile
>>> p = Profile.from_dict({"rule": [{"match": ["crowsnest", "triage"],
...     "argv": ["crowsnest", "triage"], "flags": ["-q", "--quiet"]}]})
>>> calls = []
>>> tools = mk_tools(p, runner=lambda req: calls.append(req) or Result(0, "ok", ""))
>>> [t.__name__ for t in tools]
['crowsnest_triage']
>>> tools[0](quiet=True)
'ok'
>>> calls
['crowsnest triage --quiet']
```

The runner is the seam. [`local_runner()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.local_runner) (the default) runs the gate on this machine;
[`ssh_runner()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.ssh_runner) sends the request over SSH to a key whose forced command is the gate,
which is how a process running as its own account reaches a machine’s tools without
holding any of their credentials. Building the server needs `fastmcp`
(`pip install 'hatchway[mcp]'`); nothing else in hatchway imports it.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MAX_CHARS`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.DFLT_MAX_CHARS)        | how many characters of a command's output one tool call returns; the rest is paged                                                |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_CLASSES`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.DFLT_CLASSES)          | reading only                                                                                                                      |
| [`REFUSED`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.REFUSED)               | the gate's exit statuses a runner may see                                                                                         |
| [`BUSY`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.BUSY)                  | the gate's exit statuses a runner may see                                                                                         |
| [`DFLT_FAN_OUT_DEADLINE`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.DFLT_FAN_OUT_DEADLINE) | how long one machine of a [`fan_out()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.fan_out) may take before it is named as not answering |
| [`DFLT_FAN_OUT_TTL`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.DFLT_FAN_OUT_TTL)      | how long a merged answer is reused for the same request, so its pages hold still                                                  |
| [`LATE`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.LATE)                  | the exit status of a part that missed its deadline (the far side may still be running)                                            |

### hatchway.mcp.fan_out(runners, \*, label=<function tag_lines>, is_down=<function unreachable>, deadline=25.0, ttl=30.0, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Ask every runner at once and merge their answers, each part labelled with its name.

Where [`with_fallback()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.with_fallback) asks a second machine only when the first is down,
`fan_out` asks all of them, for questions every machine answers about itself (its
own sessions). The parts come back in the order of `runners`, each through
`label` (default [`tag_lines()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.tag_lines)). A part that could not be reached, was refused,
was busy, failed, or took longer than `deadline` seconds does not fail the call: it
is named on a line of its own at the end, so the reader knows whose answer is missing
rather than reading a partial list as whole. A part that answered nothing is named too.

The call fails only when no part answered: then the status is a refusal if any part
refused, else the first part’s that reached its machine, and the error names every part.

The merged answer is reused for `ttl` seconds for the same request, so a long answer
read page by page (`offset`) does not shift under the reader. `ttl=0` turns it off.
Only use `fan_out` for reads: a request that changes something must go to one runner.

```pycon
>>> up = lambda r: Result(0, "busy  a\n", "")
>>> down = lambda r: Result(UNREACHABLE, "", "ssh: connect to host x: Operation timed out")
>>> print(fan_out({"mac": down, "tw": up})("crowsnest roster").out, end="")
[tw] busy  a
[mac] (did not answer: ssh: connect to host x: Operation timed out)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Result`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.Result)]

### hatchway.mcp.local_runner(, agent='mcp', profile=None, timeout=150, busy_retries=6)

Run each request through `hatchway gate` on this machine, as this user.

A subprocess rather than a function call, so the gate’s lock, log and timeout behave
exactly as they do behind sshd.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Result`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.Result)]

### hatchway.mcp.mk_server(profile=None, , runner=None, settings=None, classes=('read',), max_chars=6000, name=None, instructions=None, \*\*server_kwargs)

A `FastMCP` server over `profile`’s rules.

`runner` defaults to [`local_runner()`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.local_runner) with the same profile. `server_kwargs`
go to `FastMCP` (`auth=`, `middleware=`): authentication belongs to whoever
serves this over a network, not to hatchway.

### hatchway.mcp.mk_tool(rule, , runner, max_chars=6000)

One callable for `rule`, with a real signature, so any MCP host can type it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)

The tools for every rule of `profile` in one of `classes`, in profile order.

A class left out is not offered at all; one offered is still decided by the gate,
so a gated class whose flag is absent answers “refused” rather than running.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)]

### hatchway.mcp.routed_runner(default, routes)

Send a request to the runner of the longest leading words it matches in `routes`.

A key is one word or several separated by spaces; the longest key that the request’s
first words match wins, else `default`. So one server can answer about sessions from
every machine and about one store from one: `routed_runner(server, {"crowsnest":
fan_out(...), "crowsnest intent": server})`.

```pycon
>>> run = routed_runner(lambda r: "default", {"a": lambda r: "a", "a b": lambda r: "a b"})
>>> run("a b c"), run("a c"), run("ab"), run("z")
('a b', 'a', 'default', 'default')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Result`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.Result)]

### hatchway.mcp.ssh_runner(destination, , identity=None, ssh=('ssh', '-T', '-o', 'BatchMode=yes', '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=8'), timeout=150, busy_retries=6)

Send each request over SSH to `destination`, whose key’s forced command is the gate.

The request travels as the remote command, which sshd hands to the forced command as
`$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`; it is never run by a remote shell.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Result`](_autosummary/hatchway.mcp.html.md#hatchway.mcp.Result)]

### hatchway.mcp.tag_lines(name, text)

Every non-blank line of `text` prefixed with `[name]`, so merged rows say whose they are.

```pycon
>>> print(tag_lines("tw", "busy  a\n\nidle  b"), end="")
[tw] busy  a

[tw] idle  b
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hatchway.mcp.tool_name(rule)

The MCP name of a rule: its `tool` key, else its words joined by underscores.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hatchway.mcp.unreachable(result)

Whether `result` is ssh failing to connect, as opposed to the far side answering.

Only then is it safe to ask someone else: the request never reached the gate, so it
ran nowhere. A timeout is not that (the command may have run), and neither is a
remote command that happened to exit 255.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### hatchway.mcp.with_fallback(primary, fallback, \*, note="(the first machine did not answer; this is the fallback's view)\\n", is_down=<function unreachable>)

`primary`, unless it could not be reached; then `fallback`, with `note` first.

# _autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md

# hatchway.policy

The allowlist: which command lines an outside agent may run, decided without running anything.

A *profile* is data (a TOML file) listing *rules*. A rule names the words the agent
sends (`match`), what actually runs (`argv`), and exactly which extra flags and
positional arguments it may add. Everything not described is refused. Deciding is a
pure function of the request string, the profile and a little context (which flag
files exist, which directories dispatch may use), so it is tested without a shell.

```pycon
>>> profile = Profile.from_dict({
...     "rule": [
...         {"match": ["crowsnest", "triage"], "argv": ["crowsnest", "triage", "-a"],
...          "flags": ["-q", "--json"]},
...     ]
... })
>>> decide("crowsnest triage -q", profile).argv
('crowsnest', 'triage', '-a', '-q')
>>> decide("crowsnest triage; rm -rf ~", profile).allowed
False
```

### Functions

| [`decide`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.decide)(request, profile, \*[, flags_present, ...])   | Decide what to do with `request` (the agent's command line, as SSH hands it).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`describe`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.describe)(profile)                                    | One line per rule, for the `help` answer an agent gets.                         |

### Classes

| [`Decision`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Decision)(allowed, request[, reason, rule, ...])   | What the gate does with a request: run `argv`, print `path`, or refuse.                                                |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Profile`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Profile)(rules[, classes, name, snapshot, ...])    | A named set of rules plus the gating of their classes.                                                                 |
| [`Rule`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Rule)(match[, argv, kind, klass, flags, ...])      | One allowed command shape.                                                                                             |
| [`ValueFlag`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.ValueFlag)(names[, pattern, free, ...])            | A flag that takes one value, checked against `pattern` (or free text, or a directory under one of the dispatch roots). |

### *class* hatchway.policy.Decision(allowed, request, reason='', rule=None, argv=(), path='', stdin=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What the gate does with a request: run `argv`, print `path`, or refuse.

### *class* hatchway.policy.Profile(rules, classes=dict(), name='', snapshot=(), instructions='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A named set of rules plus the gating of their classes.

#### rule_for(tokens)

The rule with the longest `match` that prefixes `tokens`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Rule`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Rule) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *class* hatchway.policy.Rule(match, argv=(), kind='exec', klass='read', flags=frozenset({}), value_flags=(), max_positional=0, min_positional=0, positional_pattern='[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@:+-]{0,127}', root='', help='', tool='', arg='', param='', stdin='', reply='', tail=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One allowed command shape.

`kind` is `exec` (run `argv` plus the checked extras) or `file` (print one
file, named by the single positional argument, from the directory `root`).
`klass` groups rules for gating: a class listed in the profile’s `[classes]`
table with `requires_flag` is refused until that flag file exists.

`tool`, `param` and `arg` only name things for other transports (the MCP
tool’s name, its positional parameter’s name and that parameter’s description); `stdin` names a `free` value flag
whose value is written to the command’s standard input instead of its arguments,
so a body of text (a note to publish) never lands in `argv`. `reply` shapes a
successful answer for those transports: a template whose only field is `{out}`, the
command’s output stripped (a published link turned into a line to paste elsewhere).
`tail` is fixed words placed after the request’s arguments (`-`, for a command
that reads its text from standard input only in that position).

### *class* hatchway.policy.ValueFlag(names, pattern='[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@:+-]{0,127}', free=False, path_under_roots=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A flag that takes one value, checked against `pattern` (or free text, or a
directory under one of the dispatch roots).

### hatchway.policy.decide(request, profile, , flags_present=frozenset({}), dispatch_roots=(), roots=None)

Decide what to do with `request` (the agent’s command line, as SSH hands it).

`flags_present` names the flag files that exist (a gated class needs its flag);
`dispatch_roots` are the directories a `path_under_roots` value must sit in;
`roots` maps a file rule’s `root` name to a directory.

```pycon
>>> p = Profile.from_dict({"rule": [
...     {"match": ["snapshot"], "kind": "file", "root": "out"}]})
>>> decide("snapshot ../../.ssh/id_ed25519", p, roots={"out": "/tmp/o"}).allowed
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Decision`](_autosummary/hatchway.policy.html.md#hatchway.policy.Decision)

### hatchway.policy.describe(profile)

One line per rule, for the `help` answer an agent gets.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`hatchway` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `hatchway`

Connect an outside agent (a personal assistant on its own cloud VM such as Meta’s Muse, another machine’s scheduler, a phone shortcut) to the tools on this machine through one confined SSH key: `hatchway authorize` writes a forced-command authorized_keys line, the gate runs only an allowlist kept as a TOML profile, every call is logged, and a snapshot keeps the answers on disk. Use when asked to “let my assistant read my sessions”, “give my assistant access to crowsnest”, “set up a bridge”, “allow an agent to SSH in but only run X”, “forced command”, “restricted SSH key”, “lock down an agent’s access”, “what did the agent run”, “revoke the agent”, and to add a rule, a profile or a gated class. Not for exposing tools over MCP or HTTP (a different surface, not yet built).

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/hatchway hatchway --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`hatchway/data/skills/hatchway`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/hatchway/tree/HEAD/hatchway/data/skills/hatchway) (bundled with the pip package).

### `hatchway-muse`

Recognise when a task would be better handed to a personal Muse agent (Meta’s consumer agent with its own cloud VM, reachable by phone and chat) than done in a Claude Code session, pick the integration pattern that fits (hatchway SSH gate, custom MCP connector, Tailscale, a published connector, Poppy, the Gadget SDK, or Meta’s Model API for models), and write the exact prompt to paste to the agent. Use when a session meets non-code work (follow-ups, deadlines, email, calendar, bookings, purchases, monitoring prices or listings, waiting on hold, recurring digests), when the user mentions Muse, “my Meta agent”, “personal agent”, “can my assistant do this”, “hand this to my agent”, “muse connector”, “Meta Model API”, “muse-spark”, “muse-wonder”, or wants their own product reachable by personal agents.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/hatchway hatchway-muse --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`hatchway/data/skills/hatchway-muse`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/hatchway/tree/HEAD/hatchway/data/skills/hatchway-muse) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install hatchway`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/hatchway/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/hatchway/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`hatchway.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/hatchway/hatchway.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/hatchway/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
